newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudanese politician goes home from Egyptian exile.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese politician goes home from Egyptian exile.

text.p: A prominent Sudanese politician returned home on Tuesday after eight years of self-imposed exile in Cairo, state radio said.
Sherif Zein al-Abdin al-Hindi, a former leader of the influential Democratic Unionist Party (DUP), received a huge popular reception on his arrival in Khartoum, it said.
But the DUP in exile in Cairo, a pillar of the opposition to the Islamist-military government in Khartoum, dissociated itself from Hindi's decision to go home.

"He hasn't worked with us since the military coup in 1989 and he is not in the party executive. We have already said that if he goes back, he goes back by himself," party spokesman Mohammad al-Mutasim Hakim told Reuters in Cairo.
Before the coup Hindi had been deputy prime minister, foreign minister and secretary general of the DUP.
He had recently held talks abroad with Sudanese government figures, including President Omar Hassan al-Bashir in Cairo during an Arab summit in 1996.

Hindi is the second prominent political leader to return to Sudan in recent years. Former security chief al-Hadi Bushra went home in 1995, won a seat in parliament and was appointed communications minister last year.
